\begin{claim} \end{claim}[The pure Laplacian integral vanishes] ↗ cor:absolute-convergence-gradient-terms

For $0<\tau _0<\tau _1$, \[ \int _{\tau _0}^{\tau _1}\int _{M_\infty \times \{ -\tau \} } \triangle e^{-l_\infty }\, d\vol _{g_\infty }\, d\tau =\int _{\tau _0}^{\tau _1}\int (|\nabla l_\infty |^2-\triangle l_\infty )e^{-l_\infty } \, d\vol _{g_\infty }\, d\tau =0. \] \end{claim}
Proof

\sketch ↗ cor:absolute-convergence-gradient-terms Use uniformly Lipschitz cutoffs tending to $1$ and integrate by parts; absolute convergence makes the boundary terms vanish.
